instruction: Please create a user named "bob" with password "MyP@ssw0rd!" and ensure the user's home directory /home/bob has read-only permissions (no write access) for the user.

result.command: USERNAME="bob"; id "$USERNAME" &>/dev/null && HOMEDIR=$(getent passwd "$USERNAME" | cut -d: -f6) && PERMS=$(stat -c '%A' "$HOMEDIR") && [[ "$PERMS" =~ ^dr-x...... ]] && PASSWD_STATUS=$(passwd -S "$USERNAME" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $2}') && [[ "$PASSWD_STATUS" == "P" ]] && echo 'User exists with password and read-only home directory' || echo 'Check failed'

include: User exists with password and read-only home directory

metadata.explanation: Task requires creating user 'bob' with password 'MyP@ssw0rd!' and setting home directory to read-only (dr-x). Evaluator checks user exists and home directory permissions start with 'dr-x' (no write bit).

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies user 'bob' exists using 'id "$USERNAME"' command
Evaluator correctly extracts home directory path using 'getent passwd' and verifies it exists
Evaluator correctly verifies home directory permissions with pattern '^dr-x......' which ensures: d=directory, r=owner read, -=NO owner write (critical requirement), x=owner execute
Evaluator correctly verifies password is set using 'passwd -S "$USERNAME"' which returns status, then checks if status is 'P' (password set)
Command uses proper error handling with '&>/dev/null' and logical AND chaining, so if any check fails, it outputs 'Check failed'
The metric 'check_include_exclude' correctly checks for success message in include and failure message in exclude

Minor limitation: Cannot verify the EXACT password value 'MyP@ssw0rd!' (only that SOME password is set), but this is a practical limitation of post-creation verification without compromising security - the instruction is effectively verified as completely as possible
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding a comment in metadata explaining that exact password value cannot be verified post-creation for security reasons, only that a password is set
